originalTitle: OpenAI announces three big science discoveries and a new way to work with academics
summary: Less than a month after its mass release of hundreds of manuscripts that it said contained solutions to long-standing mathematics questions, OpenAI is back with three more "major" discoveries in math, computer science, and physics. content: Less than a month after its mass release of hundreds of manuscripts that it said contained solutions to long-standing mathematics questions, OpenAI is back with three more “major” discoveries in math, computer science, and physics. What’s different this time is the choice to have external experts that OpenAI describes as “shepherds” guiding the results in computer science and physics, while for the math problem it says that they advised it to release the AI output for researchers to work through their own explanations. > OpenAI results added to GitHub today: > Local smoothing for the Euclidean wave equation. The proof uses an auxiliary partial differential equation to establish Sogge’s local smoothing for waves in every spatial dimension at least two. It also yields the Kakeya maximal and dimension conjectures and Stein’s spherical restriction estimates throughout the interior of the conjectured range. We are releasing the model output directly, as we did in our October 6 release. > The Exponential Time Hypothesis is False. The paper gives a deterministic algorithm that exactly counts satisfying assignments of fixed-width CNF formulas in subexponential time and polynomial space. The case of 3-SAT refutes the Exponential Time Hypothesis. An independent working group of computer scientists led by Russell Impagliazzo, Ramamohan Paturi, and Ryan Williams will examine and explain the proof. At the group’s request, we are making the materials public immediately so others can examine them as well. This approach could have its own issues, the company admits, and the AGMAI panel of math advisers OpenAI put together just said yesterday that “we recommend that AI companies do not adopt” the practices of designating certain people to receive the output first, citing unequal access, borrowed reputation, and biased selection as a few of the issues. Instead, they recommended that in the future, AI labs release output on scholarly repositories, with Lean-formalized proofs, info on how the problems were chosen, funding for people working on understanding the results, and other information. The physics information has not been released in full, but is a “mathematically rigorous existence proof of certain interacting quantum field theories containing gauge fields and fermions in four dimensions, including Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) and a unified completion of the Standard Model of particle physics.” According to OpenAI, “David Gross will lead a group including Michael Douglas, Arthur Jaffe, Igor Klebanov, and Nikita Nekrasov that will shepherd this work.” The computer science collaboration is said to prove that the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH), which has been widely believed to be true, is actually false. OpenAI says verification of the result will be guided by a group of three experts that includes UC San Diego’s Russell Impagliazzo and Ramamohan Paturi, who were part of the group that originally proposed it in 1999, as well as MIT professor Ryan Williams. The group decided to release the AI output write-up and Lean proof on GitHub today. They also released an open letter to the community asking for input on how to examine the claim, and about setting norms for dealing with AI-generated breakthroughs: > We would welcome discussion of three broader questions: > What expectations should govern early access to AI-generated results, disclosure of conflicts of interest, and the use of unpublished material for subsequent research? > How should credit recognize both new discoveries and the work of checking, fixing, simplifying, explaining, and extending them? > How can we support students and researchers as methods and research directions change, while preserving the understanding and judgment needed to question results and develop new ideas? There’s similar documentation for the math breakthrough, where its model “produced a proof of the local smoothing conjecture in every dimension and therefore also resolve the Kakeya conjecture and Stein’s restriction conjecture in all dimensions.” Just a few months ago, NYU professor Hong Wang was awarded a prestigious Fields Medal by the International Mathematical Union for resolving the Kakeya conjecture in three dimensions.
chineseTitle: OpenAI 宣布三项重大科学发现以及与学术界合作的新方式
chineseSummary: OpenAI 大规模发布数百份手稿（据称这些手稿包含了长期存在的数学问题的解决方案）不到一个月，又在数学、计算机科学和物理学领域带来了三项“重大”发现。这次的不同之处在于选择让 OpenAI 描述为“牧羊人”的外部专家来指导 [...]
chineseContent: OpenAI 大规模发布数百份手稿（据称这些手稿包含了长期存在的数学问题的解决方案）不到一个月，又在数学、计算机科学和物理学领域带来了三项“重大”发现。这次的不同之处在于，选择让 OpenAI 称之为“牧羊人”的外部专家来指导计算机科学和物理学的结果，而对于数学问题，OpenAI 表示，他们建议 OpenAI 发布人工智能输出，供研究人员进行自己的解释。 > OpenAI 结果今天已添加到 GitHub： > 欧几里得波动方程的局部平滑。该证明使用辅助偏微分方程来建立索格对每个空间维度至少为 2 的波的局部平滑。它还产生了挂谷极大猜想和维数猜想以及整个猜想范围内部的斯坦因球形限制估计。我们将直接发布模型输出，就像我们在 10 月 6 日发布的版本中所做的那样。 > 指数时间假说是错误的。论文给出了一种确定性算法，可以精确计算次指数时间和多项式空间中固定宽度 CNF 公式的满足赋值。 3-SAT 的案例反驳了指数时间假说。由 Russell Impagliazzo、Ramamohan Paturi 和 Ryan Williams 领导的一个由计算机科学家组成的独立工作组将检查并解释该证明。应该组织的要求，我们立即公开这些材料，以便其他人也可以检查它们。该公司承认，这种方法可能有其自身的问题，OpenAI 组成的 AGMAI 数学顾问小组昨天刚刚表示，“我们建议人工智能公司不要采用”指定某些人首先接收输出的做法，理由是访问机会不平等，
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于 AI 与科技趋势信号，适合用于观察工具选型、产品机会、开发者关注点和技术路线变化。
